---
name: number-game-ceiling
description: Rule+interval+digit concept model is near its ceiling; single-param tweaks gain only 3-6 nats in-sample
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 1 (iter_1, candidate_5) MAP screens with equal-weight 44-rule + uniform-interval model (in-sample NLL 912): free example-noise 908.5, lapse 907.9, noise+lapse 906.3, logit response map 908.6, size-principle exponent 911.6, Erlang interval prior 913.5 (uniform is better), rule-family weights about 911, free 45 weights 893 (but the extra params cost it on LOO). Calibration by predicted-p bin is already good. Biggest per-set residuals: 83,38,58,68 (scattered 20-40% yes in the 50s-70s), 85,19,91 (odd numbers overpredicted), 14,47.
Submitted `equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse` (the lapse model with one shared rule prior): smoke loglik -905.8.

**Why:** the next improvement probably needs a new mechanism, not another response or prior parameter. Builds on [[digit-concepts-key]].
**How to apply:** don't spend rounds on noise/lapse/exponent tweaks; look at the residual sets above.

Round 2 cand_5 (2026-10-30) numpy MAP screens on the incumbent (NLL 904.5): strong/weak sampling mix 904.5 (no gain), bonus for round-boundary (decade) intervals 904.5, lapse drifting with trial_index 904.3, guess-yes drift 904.5, rule prior ∝ size^-g 903.3 (g≈0.25), all-hypothesis prior ∝ size^-g 902.7. Submitted `specificity_biased_rule_prior_lapse` (rule-only version, smoke loglik -904.7). Data = 5 sessions × 450 trials, contiguous in the CSV (trial_index resets), n=5 per cell, so most residual is binomial noise. Reusable screener: a numpy set × hypothesis log-lik matrix with Nelder-Mead runs in about 1 min per variant.
---
name: iter3-process-screens
description: Round 3 screens of new process families (memory, carry-over, log number line, pedagogical) all tie the base; Chebyshev-in-parameter trick makes heavy models ~0.3 ms/grad
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3, candidate_2 (2026-10-30), MAP screens on equal_prior+lapse (NLL 904.52):
- Random forgetting of examples: forget rate goes to 0, no gain.
- Carry-over of the previous trial's set or target into the current one: c goes to 0. Trials are interleaved, and there are only 450 distinct (set, target) cells × 5 sessions.
- Power/log compressed number line for intervals: log is worse (+19 nats); the best exponent is about 1.13, a gain of 0.3.
- Pedagogical teacher, P(x|h) ∝ P(h|x)^α: α≈0.05-0.2, gain at most 0.1. I submitted it as `pedagogical_sampling_concepts` (smoke loglik -906.4; RMSE vs base about 0.005 at α=0.19).

Speed trick: when the only nonlinear parameter enters the hypothesis likelihoods, tabulate per-set and per-cell log-summed rule and interval likelihoods at Chebyshev nodes in `prepare_observed` (degree 16, error about 1e-10). λ then enters exactly via logaddexp. This took logp+grad from 171 ms to 0.3 ms.

**Why:** this confirms [[number-game-ceiling]]. New process families tie at best.
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these. Use the Chebyshev tabulation for any one-parameter likelihood change (see [[fit-speed-budget]]).
---
name: iter3-noise-ceiling-wor
description: Round 3 cand_5: incumbent is at the binomial noise ceiling; participants homogeneous; without-replacement sampling ties incumbent with 0 extra params
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3 candidate_5 (2026-10-30). The CSV has 5 participants (trial_index resets every 450 rows), and each one answers all 450 (set, target) cells once. Their yes rates run from 0.24 to 0.28.

MAP screens on `rule_breadth_prior_concepts` (NLL 903.26):
- per-person lambda_0: 902.5
- per-person gamma: 902.8
- per-person lapse + guess rate (10 extra params): 900.65
- per-person example noise (5 extra params): 900.9

So the data show no individual differences. The incumbent's NLL is 903.3, against a saturated per-cell NLL of 703.8. That excess of about 200 nats is below the roughly 225 expected from pure binomial noise, so the model is at the noise ceiling.

Submitted `without_replacement_size_principle`: the equal-prior lapse model, with each member example drawn without replacement (probability 1/(|h| - earlier member examples)). It adds no parameter. MAP NLL was 903.26, the same as the incumbent, which has one more parameter. Prediction RMSE against both models is about 0.013. Smoke loglik was -904.9.

**Why:** at the noise ceiling, only parsimony can win ELPD.
**How to apply:** don't screen participant-level structure again. See [[number-game-ceiling]] and [[iter2-screens]].
---
name: fit-speed-budget
description: Admission fit is 7000 iters/chain warm-start NUTS; per-gradient cost must be ~<25ms; tricks that worked
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1d82c78b-0bac-4618-97c8-da7bd32baa1b
  modified: 2026-10-30T21:06:41.047Z
---

Admission fits use production draws 4000 + tune 3000 per chain (warm_start_nuts, dense mass matrix), 30-min limit per run. Machine has 1 core. Incumbent `tenenbaum_digit_concepts` logp+grad ≈ 12 ms. A memory-subset mixture over its hypothesis space (≈700 states) cost 62 ms naive → too slow (~49 min).

**Why:** the check_candidate smoke fit (200 iters) passes even when the full fit would time out.

**How to apply:** benchmark logp+dlogp time and NUTS n_steps (probe `_warm_start_sample` with small draws) before finishing. Speedups that worked: replace gathering posterior rows per cell (slow AdvancedIncSubtensor1 gradient) with a `pytensor.sparse.CSR` + `structured_dot` (44→25 ms); declaring module-level `SAMPLER_SETTINGS = {"target_accept": 0.9}` halves steps (10.8→5.3). Don't name a scratch script `timeit.py` (shadows stdlib, breaks pymc import). Related: [[digit-concepts-key]].

Also worked (2026-10-30, `order_weighted_concept_learning`): when intervals must be grouped by (size, per-position hit pattern) instead of (size, k), keep only each set's non-empty groups (≤473 of 1600 on this data) padded per set, and gather size-dependent terms by index — 47 → 18 ms.
---
name: iter4-critique-proxy-stats
description: Iter-4 critique trick — PPC stats can embed a fixed-param Bayesian proxy (stimulus-only, cached) to slice by predicted probability; no iter 0-3 stat was ever significant
metadata:
  type: project
---
Through iter 0-3 no PPC statistic reached p<=0.05. The near-misses were trial-index slope (p=0.05), cell unanimity (p=0.06) and in-set target yes (observed 0.68 vs 0.74). All 5 participants see the same trial order.

Iter 4 (2026-10-30) stats embed `_proxy(df)`: rules+intervals, gamma=0, lambda=0.5, WOR, no lapse. It depends only on the stimuli and is cached in a module dict, so it takes about 1 ms per call. The stats slice by its q: ambiguous band, confident members, late-vs-early false alarms, false-alarm cell overdispersion, single-example correlation. Three new relation stats: digit reversal, double/half, digit-sum.

**How to apply:** reuse the proxy template from iter_4/critique/test_stats; check ppc_results there before re-proposing. See [[iter3-noise-ceiling-wor]].

---
name: iter3-concept-family-screens
description: Round 3 cand_0 screens of extra concept families on rule_breadth_prior_concepts (NLL 903.26); all at ceiling; submitted counting_by_twos_run_concepts
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3, candidate_0 (2026-10-30). Baseline is rule_breadth_prior_concepts, MAP NLL 903.26. None of these extra families gained anything (best family weight → -inf): residue classes mod 3-12 with nonzero offsets; bounded arithmetic progressions with steps 2-10 or 2-20; rule ∩ contiguous range (6003 concepts). Two families came out flat, neither gaining nor losing. Step-2 runs ("counting by twos") gave 903.18 with family mass e^-3 of the rules, and runs of multiples of 10 gave 903.22. The all-steps AP family *hurts* at share ≥ e^-3, by 2.6 nats or more.

I submitted `counting_by_twos_run_concepts`, which is the incumbent plus step-2 runs, with log_run_share ~ N(-3, 1.5). Smoke loglik was -905.0 and the check took about 3 s per 200 iterations. Novelty RMSE against the incumbent is 0.006 at share -4 and 0.014 at -3, so it clears the 0.002 gate.

**Why:** this confirms [[number-game-ceiling]] and [[iter2-screens]]. Concept-space additions can't move the fit.
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these families. Note the screener bug: noise term is 0.1/100 = 0.001, not 0.01.
---
name: iter2-screens
description: Round 2 MAP screens on equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse (NLL 904.5): new concept families and response tweaks gain at most ~1.8 nats
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 2, candidate_4 (2026-10-30). Baseline in-sample NLL 904.5. Adding decade, repdigit, digit-sum, single-digit or "contains both digits" rules gave no gain. Logit sharpening gave 0. Free example noise gave 902.7, but lapse then drops to about 0.008, so it would duplicate `digit_concepts_inferred_outlier_rate`. A rule prior proportional to |rule|^gamma gave 903.3 with gamma≈-0.24, a slight preference for narrow rules. I submitted that as `rule_breadth_prior_concepts`. Its smoke loglik was -904.8 and the fit took about 2 s per 200 iterations.

**Why:** this confirms [[number-game-ceiling]]. Most of the residual is 5-response-per-cell binomial noise.
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these concept families. Further gains are unlikely without participant-level structure, and the CSV has no participant column.

Round 2 cand_5 repair (2026-10-30): `specificity_biased_rule_prior_lapse` was rejected as a near-duplicate of `rule_breadth_prior_concepts` (RMSE 0.0003). The repair is `occam_specificity_prior_all_concepts`, which applies the same |c|^-g to intervals too, normalised within each class and collapsed to 100 size groups per set. Smoke loglik was -904.4, about 16 s per 200 iterations. Applying g to intervals moves p_yes by RMSE ≈ 0.01 at g = 0.1, which clears the 0.002 novelty gate.
---
name: iter3-screens
description: Round 3 MAP screens on rule_breadth_prior_concepts (NLL 903.3); sampling without replacement +0.5 nats with 0 params, submitted
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3, candidate_4 (2026-10-30). Baseline numpy MAP NLL was 903.3. Fuzzy interval edges gave 903.2. A log-quadratic breadth prior gave 902.8 (+1 param). Scaling gamma by the number of examples gave 903.3, and gamma divided by n gave 904.0. Strong sampling *without replacement* gave 902.8 with no new parameter. Its prediction RMSE against the incumbent is 0.0074 (largest change at 8,64 → 16), so it clears the novelty gate. I submitted it as `concepts_sampled_without_replacement`, with smoke loglik -904.3 and about 3 s per 200 iterations. The screener script is in iter_3/candidate_4/scratch/s/.

**Why:** this confirms [[number-game-ceiling]] again. Residual sets (14,47; 83,38,58,68; 85,19,91) look like binomial noise.
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these forms. Candidate_3 refined the same incumbent in parallel this round.

distinct draws from the concept (strong sampling without replacement), 10% of

uniformly. Round numbers (multiples of 5) carry a production weight exp(b)
relative to other numbers, and b (its sign and size) is inferred. So the k-th
example x is drawn with probability
    0.9 * [x in h] w(x) / (W(h) - weight of h's members already shown)
    + 0.1 * w(x) / W(1..100).

makes a round example more or less informative than a non-round one.

tabulated in prepare_observed as a Chebyshev series in b over [-B_MAX, B_MAX].

import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt
from numpy.polynomial import chebyshev as cheb

B_MAX = 2.0
DEGREE = 16
NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)

        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),

    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return list(rules.values())

I've submitted **`round_number_salient_sampling`**. It passes the admission check, but in-sample it beats the current best model by only about 0.5 nats while adding one parameter, so on ELPD-LOO it will most likely tie or fall slightly behind.

**Hypothesis:** people learn concepts the same way as the current best model, `concepts_sampled_without_replacement`. The one new claim is that they don't think the program picks numbers uniformly. They think round numbers (multiples of 5) come out more or less often than other numbers, and the model infers how strong that bias is and which way it goes. That weighting applies both to examples drawn from the concept and to the occasional random stray example.

**Check result:** `OK`. The log-likelihood on the smoke fit was -904.1, and sampling took about 2 seconds per 200 iterations, well inside the 30-minute limit. Its predictions differ from the best model's by RMSE 0.011 on the novelty pool, well above the 0.002 near-duplicate cutoff. The check can't confirm convergence because it runs one chain; the full fit will show that.

**What I tried first.** All of these were quick best-fit screens on the current best model (in-sample NLL 902.77):
- **Weighting by magnitude** (smaller numbers more likely to be shown): uniform sampling is clearly best, and any tilt costs 2–4 nats.
- **Round-number weighting:** best fit with round numbers slightly *less* likely to be shown, giving 902.21. This is the one I submitted.
- **Weighting multiples of 10 or single-digit numbers:** gained at most 0.3 nats.
- **Growing or shrinking belief in rules over the session** (using `trial_index`): no gain. It also couldn't pass the near-duplicate check, because the novelty pool has no `trial_index` column.

The critique found no significant discrepancy in the best model, and earlier notes put it at the noise level of the data. Each (set, target) pair gets only 5 answers.

Files are in `experiment1/model_loop/iter_4/candidate_1/`:
- `hypothesis.md`
- `model_name.txt`
- `candidate.py`

I also added a memory note so future rounds don't repeat these screens.
